title: Indiana's 6th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Indiana's 6th Congressional District is holding a general election on November 3, 2026, to elect a U.S. Representative. The district covers 11 counties across central and eastern Indiana, including parts of southern Marion County and the city of Columbus. First-term Republican incumbent Jefferson Shreve, who won the seat in 2024 after the retirement of Greg Pence, narrowly defeated a primary challenger with 53% of the vote. He will face Democratic nominee Cynthia "Cinde" Wirth in a rematch of their 2024 contest, which Shreve won by more than 30 points. The Cook Political Report rates this race as Solidly Republican, and control of the U.S. House adds to the national significance of this contest.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date.

candidates.name: Jefferson Shreve
candidates.summary: Jefferson Shreve is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Indiana's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A businessman who founded and sold Storage Express for $590 million, he previously served on the Indianapolis City-County Council and was the Republican nominee for Mayor of Indianapolis in 2023. In Congress, he serves on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and has focused on border security and fiscal issues.

candidates.name: Cynthia Wirth
candidates.summary: Cynthia "Cinde" Wirth is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 6th Congressional District. She is a small business owner, field scientist, and former public high school teacher who earned her PhD in cultural and educational policy from Ball State University in 2025. A first-generation college graduate and seventh-generation resident of Bartholomew County, Wirth previously served as a congressional fellow in Washington, D.C., and lost to Jefferson Shreve in the 2024 general election. Her campaign priorities include universal single-payer health care, raising wages, and government accountability.
